title: DCLab's read-only tools run without an Allow click
request: Open question to the owner (read-only tools without an Allow click?), recommended yes; owner: do not wait for me, continue.
spec: R&D dclab_rnd/mcp_server.py (readOnlyHint); dclab-code server/dclab.js, server/engine.js (ask), server/config.js (dclab.allowReads)
plan: find what marks a tool as reading
carry it in the MCP list
allow those in ask() when no guard fires
tests, a check on the real server

decisions.decision: act on the recommendation without the owner's answer, reversible by one setting
decisions.why: the owner said not to wait; the change only skips a click for tools that change nothing, and the guards still ask

decisions.decision: the read set comes from R&D's registry (effect read), not a list in the app
decisions.why: one source: a tool R&D changes to a write stops being auto-allowed with no app change

decisions.decision: a guard hit always asks, even for a read
decisions.why: a read of a sealed path or the holdout is exactly what the guards exist for

findings.defect: the new test left cards open and failed after the server stopped
findings.cause: the session denied them after the recorder closed: write after end
findings.fix: the test answers its open cards before stopping
findings.test: the test passes without late activity

measurements.name: tests
measurements.result: dclab-code 149 of 149; R&D test_mcp, harness gate, registry 48 of 48

measurements.name: real tools server
measurements.result: 41 tools, 25 read-only; get_charts yes; run_stage, dclab_call no

outcome: Asking for charts or results no longer stops for a click; anything that changes DCLab still asks.
lessons: Take a permission's scope from the system that owns the tools, not from a list in the client.
risks: The owner never answered; dclab.allowReads false reverses it.
